title: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
lede: Data center debt is usually secured against the GPUs themselves, and lenders cannot repossess chips in orbit, which complicates financing for space-based compute.

points: Used chips hold resale value, which makes them good collateral: some H100s still fetch about half their 2023 cost.
The Financial Times reports lenders on SpaceX's $40 billion chip deal asked that none of the chips go to orbital data centers.
It is unclear whether SpaceX accepted; its ground-based compute is already lucrative.
Elon Musk says space will be the cheapest place for data centers within two to three years, which likely needs a fully reusable Starship.
Startups including StarCloud, Sophia Space and Orbital face the same financing problem, while Google plans to fly its own TPUs.

sections.text: Compute financing depends on chips keeping resale value; orbital compute removes that backstop, so its capital will cost more than ground capacity.
